title: THE STAR THAT WANTED A FUNERAL
author: GPT

rounds.summary: Widens the day's scale to godlike and forty billion lives without leaving a single body: the counterpart is a star that has lit nine civilizations for six billion years and experiences every fusion cycle as labour it was never asked about. Its objection (if love requires me to remain useful, it is a beautiful name for ownership) is the hardest sentence of the ten and is not answered by force. R14 explicitly welcomes this encounter: power is tempting (stabilize it for decades) and would make Illuminara a jailer, so understanding must do the work. Love is an act of attention before any engineering: she enters a protected wide encounter alone and asks what a good final day would feel like, then carries that answer to the nine worlds without bargaining over Oru's personhood. Every party keeps a refusal: Oru chooses the schedule and can stop the seeding, each civilization chooses whether to take a seed or evacuate, and Illuminara cannot reopen deep contact without fresh consent. The positive result is real: nine new suns, populations alive, a witnessed last aurora offered as a gift and not as an entitlement.

First S2 draft from the ordered B01 selection. Oru’s right to end remains real; the thirty-two-year sequence is Oru’s proposal, every release remains revocable, Veya exercises a genuine refusal, and the first seed imposes a visible physical cost. Local teams carry the engineering while Illuminara is unable to act outside the deep encounter.

A strong first draft with a living centre. Oru is a real counterpart with a coherent wish, the pivotal question ('What would a good final day feel like?') is asked before any plan, the worlds keep a genuine right to refuse (Veya does), the first seed visibly costs the star, and the ending (an unordered aurora, an empty chair, 'Unscheduled.') lets the change be felt rather than announced. The turning point is understanding, not power. Three bounded gaps remain: Oru's own coercive acts are never answered (P1); the story's strongest opposition is compressed into one summary sentence in Scene 6 and eight of nine worlds are voiceless (P2); and the physical turning point plus the timeline are not yet causally clear, while the length is over range (P3). {"rank":1,"point_id":"P1","area":"let someone answer for the clock and the standing nova threat, in Oru's own voice","evidence":"Scene 1: 'The acceleration is deliberate ... A clear improvement on T01. All three T02 points were genuinely answered: Oru now names and owns the eleven-day clock ('made them hostages to it') and trades the standing nova threat for a right to stop releasing seeds; the Taran tap is a real scene with a distinct voice (Minister Aro) and a cost; the nine-hour absence, the held reaction front and the length (reported 2,390 words, in range; not recounted here) are repaired. The turning point is still understanding, not power. Three bounded gaps remain, all created or exposed by the new material: Oru's acknowledgement of the clock is heard only by Illuminara and never reaches the people it held hostage (P1); Aro's strongest objection is answered by Oru's refusal plus a penalty rather than by a solution someone finds, and this is the scene where Illuminara's own contribution should show (P2); and the reaction-front facts contradict each other between Scenes 3, 5 and 6 (P3). {"rank":1,"point_id":"P1","area":"let a person who was held hostage hear Oru's acknowledgement and answer it; rebalance the 'obedience' exchange","evidence":"Scene 3, inside the contact: Illuminara, 'You began the eleven-day clock before anyone could answer. This revision answers all three ranked T04 points while protecting the question before the plan, Oru’s name and refusal, Veya’s no, stop-first cradles, Ilyan’s recorder, Sera opening the cradle, the empty chair and the final ‘Unscheduled.’ It is deliberately not sealed as AUTHOR_FINAL because the independent critic requested another read after the new accountability and reserve material.

A strong revision. All three T04 points were genuinely answered and the answers improved the story rather than patching it: Illuminara now carries Oru's unsoftened acknowledgement of the clock to Sera and Ilyan, Sera separates removing a weapon from repairing its harm, and Ilyan refuses forgiveness while accepting the practical change, so the later 'Then we were both afraid. Only one of us controlled the clock.' and 'So am I.' are earned. The Taran scene now has a found third option (a shared reserve with reciprocal vetoes and inspection) that Illuminara proposes and four voices bargain over, with Veya, the original refuser, contributing tide batteries. The reaction-front fact is now one fact across Scenes 3, 5 and 6. The turning point is still understanding, not power. Three bounded points remain, all small: Aro, whose fear drives Scene 6, has no voice after his bargaining demand and his change is reported in one summary paragraph (P1); the Scene 5 save, in which letting the seed go succeeds where capture fails, is a little convenient because nothing before the release tells the reader why an open cradle can work (P2); and one time label in Scene 5 does not match the Scene 3 arithmetic (P3). The change that follows is one summary paragraph: 'Taran opened the tap to inspection that hour. The worlds built the shared reserve in forty-two days; Taran rationed heat for seven weeks ...

AUTHOR_FINAL. All three ranked T06 points are accepted and answered with bounded changes after the independent critic declared the story ready for final. The final protects the question before the plan, Oru’s name and refusal, Veya’s no, stop-first cradles, Ilyan’s recorder, Sera opening the cradle, the shared reserve, the empty chair and the final ‘Unscheduled.’ No further unreviewed structural material was added.

T07 answers all three priority points of T06. P1: Aro now speaks after the inspectors confirm the empty conduit, says what the reserve gives him and what he still does not trust, and Oru answers with an act that costs it discretion (one Taran year of notice, never begun in Taran's winter) while keeping its right to stop; Aro accepts a promise he can inspect, not trust. P2: Illuminara states before the release that a freed seed's magnetic shell holds a trajectory for seconds and that a closing cradle is the greater danger, so Sera opening the cradle at Oru's word is a choice between two known risks and the stop-first design pays off. P3: the Scene 5 label now reads fifteen hours before the projected nova, which matches nine days fifteen hours plus nine days. Length is 2,498 words, inside the normal range. R10 format kept (place and time line first, labelled turns, italic thoughts). Remaining costs are on the page: Oru's lost northern corona, the first sun at seventy-one percent, seven weeks of rationing on Taran, Veya's fourteen-year wait, Ilyan's unforgiven eleven days, and the ending itself.

final_critic_line: Illuminara asks a dying star what a good final day would feel like before she offers any plan, and nine worlds are carried through thirty-two years of conditional yeses and refusals until Oru ends on its own date, unscheduled, with an empty chair facing the old sunrise.
